info.title: BrewMyJob API
info.description: Job alerts in, fit scores and tailored packs out. You always submit.

post.description: Create an account. Also creates an empty candidate profile, default notification settings and the consent record.
Rotate the refresh token (cookie for web, body for mobile) and return a new access token.

get.description: The plans and prices, and your access now. Paying comes later; an invite's coupon gives free months.
What an invite link offers (no sign-in needed: the link is the secret).

post.description: Accept an invite with the account it was made for. Refresh the session afterwards for a new role.

schema.title: Response Invites Api V1 Admin Invites Get

post.description:
Invite a job seeker (optionally with a 1- or 3-month coupon) or an admin. No email is sent yet: copy the
link and send it yourself.

get.description: The values the super admin set, for every signed-in user.

post.description: Read a resume from the library into candidate-profile fields (Claude when configured, else rules).

put.description:
Where you want to work (asked once of accounts made before sign-up asked it). Match profiles without
any location take these too.

get.description: Your match profiles, one per resume (the primary resume's first).

schema.title: Response List Profiles Api V1 Profiles Get

post.description: Read the resume's skills again (after you add a skill to the resume, say). Skills you added stay.
Add a skill you have to this profile (a job asked for it and the resume doesn't show it).

delete.description: Forget the number; messages waiting to be sent are dropped.

post.description: Save the number and send it a one-time code on WhatsApp. Alerts start once the code is entered.
Send a code to the number already saved (given at sign-up, or a new code after one expired).
Send your best open match now, as a job alert looks.

get.description: What needs your attention: new top matches, possible duplicates, follow-ups due, jobs that may have expired.

post.description: You opened the bell: everything in it now counts as read.
A new forwarding address. Mail to the old one is rejected from now on; update the Gmail filter.
Accept alerts this user forwards by hand from `address` (DKIM must pass for its domain on arrival).

post.description:
Deliver a saved alert email (.eml) as if it had been forwarded. Local development only: an uploaded
file has no verified DKIM signature, so in production it could plant fake listings in the shared catalog.

get.description:
Ready-made Google searches for LinkedIn, Naukri and Foundit job pages, from your roles for Google (the ones
Google Alerts use too; else your target roles) and job locations. You run them in your own browser; BrewMyJob
never reads those sites.

post.description:
Add a job you found on LinkedIn, Naukri or Foundit. The link is only read for the portal's job id; the
page is never opened. With the description pasted, the score is a full one.

patch.description:
Mark a job seen, ignored, applied or expired, or restore it (status "seen").

Applied records an application (you apply yourself; this keeps track). Leaving Applied removes that
application, which is refused once it has updates. Expired here is your choice and stays even when a new
alert shows the job again.

post.description:
Not for me, and why (milestone 13 A). The job is ignored. A reason about its company, city, field or level
is learned: jobs like it score at most 40 from now on (Other jobs), listed on Profile to undo.
You checked the posting and it's still open: clears "May have expired" and restarts the clock.

get.description:
How another of your resumes does on this job, factor by factor, against the same search profile as the
job's match. Nothing is saved; the suggested resume stays the one with the best score.

post.description:
Add a skill you really have to the match profile of the resume this job was matched with (its suggested
resume; else your primary resume's). This job is re-scored now, the rest in the background.

Tailored resumes and cover letters may claim only what your resumes and profiles support, so add only
skills you can back up. The match profile lists the skills its resume doesn't show yet, to add there too.

Say the job isn't a fit because of a gap (the industry, the skills…). It is re-scored at most 40 and
moves to Other jobs; DELETE undoes it.

delete.description: Take back "not a fit": the job is re-scored on its merits.

post.description: Paste the full job description from the portal. It is stored for you only, and the job is re-scored.

Say whether a possible duplicate is the same job. Same merges the two: the applied one, else the earlier
one, is kept and the other leaves your lists. Different keeps both (undoing a merge BrewMyJob made) and the
pair isn't flagged again. Returns this job as it is now (status duplicate if it was merged away).
Upload a resume (PDF, Word, OpenDocument, RTF or text) or paste its text. The first one is primary.

Upload a new version of a resume (after adding a skill to it, say). It keeps its label, primary flag and
match profile; the profile's skills are read again from the new version, the skills you added stay.

delete.description: Delete a resume and its Skill Match profile (with the skills you added there).

get.description: The original upload, exactly as it was sent.

post.description: Upload a cover letter or write one in the app. The first one is the default.
Score every job again (e.g. after editing a resume elsewhere). Runs in the background.

get.description: The common screening questions (answered from the bank, else from your profile) and your own ones.

post.description: Add your own question and answer, e.g. "Do you have a valid passport?".

put.description: Answer a common question, or change your answer to any question.

delete.description: Delete your own question, or clear a saved answer to a common one (your profile's answer applies again).

post.description: Clear a blocker: answer a question (saved to the answer bank for every job) or accept a gap.

get.description:
Your applications, follow-ups due first, then the most recent. Filter by status and by the date applied
(a day, a month or a year is a from/to range).

parameters.name: due

schema.description: Only applications with a follow-up due
schema.title: Due

parameters.description: Only applications with a follow-up due

patch.description: Move the application on (Interviewing, Offer…), set or clear a follow-up date, or correct what you sent.

post.description: A note on the timeline: who you spoke to, what's next.

Save someone you found for this job (from the posting's "Meet the hiring team", say). Saved only:
BrewMyJob never contacts anyone.
Find a company's public job board by name or careers-page link (takes a few seconds).

schema.title: Response Lookup Api V1 Sources Lookup Post

post.description:
Add a company's job board to the shared list (found by the lookup, or by its careers link, e.g. a Workday
site). Its jobs are checked straight away, in the background, and the open ones that fit reach every user.

delete.description: Take a company off the shared list. Jobs already in users' lists stay.

post.description: Check every followed company now (at most once every 10 minutes). Adzuna runs on the shared schedule.

get.description:
Every job the job search service's last run brought for you: the ones in your list (with their score) and
the ones left out, with the reason (another field, below your level, not one of your locations).

post.description: Add a job the last run left out to your list anyway. It is scored like any other job.

get.description:
Every open India job at a company you follow: the ones in your list (with their score), the ones left out
and why, and which of them its last check found.

post.description: Add an open job at a company you follow to your list anyway. It is scored like any other job.

get.description:
Every open job the job sources brought you: the last run's first, then older ones. The ones that fit are
in your list already (with their score); the others say why they were left out, and can be added.

post.description: Add a job the sources brought you (and left out) to your list. It is scored like any other job.

get.description:
Suggested Google Alerts (one per role and job location) and the feeds you added. The roles are the ones
you set (up to 5), else your Skill Match profiles' target roles.

post.description: Add a Google Alerts RSS feed by its link. It is read straight away, then three times a day.

put.description:
Set the roles (up to 5) to get Google Alerts for. An empty list goes back to your target roles. Feeds you
added stay; create alerts for the new roles from the suggestions.

delete.description: Stop reading a feed. Jobs it brought stay in your list. (Delete the alert on Google too.)

get.description: Kinds of job you said weren't for you. Jobs like these score at most 40 (Other jobs).
